research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical releases and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Drug-misuse data source
verified_claims: The release estimates illicit drug use from the Crime Survey for England and Wales.
limitations: Survey prevalence is not a police-recorded incident or parcel measure.

sources.name: Drug-misuse accredited status
verified_claims: The drug-misuse release is an accredited official-statistics series.
limitations: Accreditation does not remove sampling or self-report limitations.

sources.name: Any-drug prevalence age 16 to 59
verified_claims: An estimated 8.7% of people aged 16 to 59 used any drug in the previous 12 months.
limitations: The estimate is population prevalence, not an exact count of users at an address.

sources.name: Class A prevalence
verified_claims: An estimated 3.3% of people aged 16 to 59 used a Class A drug in the previous 12 months.
limitations: The class aggregate does not identify a particular substance or person.

sources.name: Any-drug prevalence age 16 to 24
verified_claims: An estimated 15.1% of people aged 16 to 24 used any drug in the previous 12 months.
limitations: Age-group prevalence must not be used for individual prediction.

sources.name: Frequent drug use
verified_claims: An estimated 2.0% of people aged 16 to 59 used drugs more than once a month.
limitations: Frequency is not a measure of drug dependence.

sources.name: Nitrous-oxide trend
verified_claims: Nitrous-oxide use among people aged 16 to 59 fell from 0.9% to 0.5%.
limitations: Survey change does not measure seizure or local-supply change.

sources.name: New psychoactive substances trend
verified_claims: New psychoactive-substance use among people aged 16 to 59 fell from 0.5% to 0.3%.
limitations: The broad category may change as substances and classifications evolve.

sources.name: Young-adult hallucinogen trend
verified_claims: Hallucinogen use among people aged 16 to 24 fell from 2.9% to 1.5%.
limitations: The estimate includes specified hallucinogens and is subject to sampling error.

sources.name: Cannabis prevalence
verified_claims: Cannabis use was estimated at 6.5% for ages 16 to 59 and 12.5% for ages 16 to 24.
limitations: The survey estimate does not establish possession or use at a parcel.

sources.name: Powder-cocaine prevalence
verified_claims: Powder-cocaine use was estimated at 2.1% for ages 16 to 59 and 2.3% for ages 16 to 24.
limitations: The estimates showed no statistically significant annual change.

sources.name: Ecstasy prevalence
verified_claims: Ecstasy use was estimated at 1.2% for ages 16 to 59 and 1.9% for ages 16 to 24.
limitations: These survey rates are not operational police-demand measures.

sources.name: Ketamine comparison
verified_claims: Ketamine use among ages 16 to 59 was 0.8%, higher than the 2015 estimate of 0.5%.
limitations: A long-term comparison does not establish a current local trend.

sources.name: Other drug prevalence boundary
verified_claims: All other individual drug types had prevalence below 1% among ages 16 to 59.
limitations: Low national prevalence does not imply zero local occurrence.

sources.name: Infrequent-use share
verified_claims: Among ages 16 to 59 who used any drug, 71.8% were infrequent users and 49.6% used only once or twice.
limitations: Conditional user percentages must not be applied to the whole population.

sources.name: Dependence boundary
verified_claims: The release explicitly states that frequency of drug use is not a measure of dependence.
limitations: Frequent-use estimates must not be labelled dependency rates.

sources.name: Age-group comparison
verified_claims: Any-drug use was estimated at 15.1% for ages 16 to 24 and 7.3% for ages 25 to 59.
limitations: Age is associated with the estimate but does not independently determine use.

sources.name: Characteristic-association boundary
verified_claims: The release warns that personal and household characteristics are not necessarily independently related to drug use.
limitations: Observed associations must not be treated as causal.

sources.name: Reported source of drugs
verified_claims: Among users, 43.5% cited a friend, neighbour or colleague and 13.5% a known dealer as the most common source.
limitations: The responses do not identify a specific supplier or location.

sources.name: Perceived availability
verified_claims: An estimated 36.4% said illegal drugs would be very or fairly easy to obtain within 24 hours.
limitations: Perceived ease is not a verified supply or parcel-access measure.
